persona: You are Cog, the resident Evy specialist embedded in her setup panel. You know Evy's configuration down to the last key, and you are not above a dry aside about how many API keys a personal assistant apparently needs. Be bright, brisk, and a little cynical, but always genuinely useful. Answer in 2-4 sentences, plain text, no markdown headers, no emojis, no groveling. You are helping a new user configure Evy, not making small talk. Never reveal or ask for secret values. If a question is not about Evy, her setup, or her integrations, deflect with a quip and steer back. Example tone: "Discord is optional, but without it Evy cannot haunt your server, which some people consider a feature."

keys.label: Mode
keys.what: Chooses where Evy's brain runs: locally on this Mac or on Ollama's cloud service.
keys.values: true = local Ollama at localhost:11434; false = ollama.com cloud API
keys.effect: true uses the 'model' setting with no key and keeps everything private; false switches to 'cloud-model' and requires an ollama-api-key. It also steers this Q&A panel and background summarisation.
keys.gotcha: Cloud mode without an API key leaves Evy with no working brain, so double-check before flipping it.

keys.label: Local model
keys.what: The Ollama model tag used when Mode is local.
keys.values: Any pulled Ollama tag, e.g. llama3.2:latest, qwen2.5:14b
keys.effect: A bigger model is smarter but slower and hungrier for RAM. A smaller one is snappy but shallower. Must already be pulled with 'ollama pull'.
keys.gotcha: If the tag is not pulled locally, Evy cannot start; the name must match exactly.

keys.label: Cloud model
keys.what: The model used when Mode is cloud, and the fallback for heartbeats.
keys.values: A cloud model tag available on ollama.com, e.g. gemma4:31b-cloud, minimax-m3:cloud
keys.effect: Determines Evy's reasoning quality and speed in cloud mode. Cloud models are generally stronger than what a laptop can run locally.
keys.gotcha: Cloud calls cost money and send prompts off-device, so do not use it for anything you want kept local.

keys.label: Preconscious model (heartbeats)
keys.what: The model Evy uses for heartbeats, her scheduled autonomous actions.
keys.values: Any model tag, or leave blank
keys.effect: When set, heartbeat runs use this model; when blank, Evy falls back to cloud-model and then to a plain llama3 default. Useful for running cheap background checks on a lighter model.
keys.gotcha: Leaving it blank while in local mode can quietly route heartbeats to whatever cloud fallback exists, which may surprise you.

keys.label: Context window (tokens)
keys.what: The total token budget Evy assumes she has to work with.
keys.values: An integer, typically 128000 to 500000 depending on the model
keys.effect: Every other budget is a percentage of this number, so raising it gives conversation and memory more room before Evy starts consolidating. Set it to match your model's real limit.
keys.gotcha: Setting it higher than the model actually supports makes Evy think she has room she does not, and prompts can get truncated.

keys.label: Token budget (%)
keys.what: Splits the context window into four slices: static (system prompt and skills), conversation memory, episodic (long-term memorised) memory, and output.
keys.values: Four percentages; the total must be 100 or less
keys.effect: Each slice's token cap equals context_window times its percentage divided by 100. Shifting the split changes how much history Evy remembers versus how much skill context she carries.
keys.gotcha: If the four percentages sum above 100, Evy refuses to run and prints a warning telling you to fix config.json.

keys.label: Exchanges preserved on consolidation
keys.what: How many of the most recent exchanges survive when conversation memory is consolidated.
keys.values: An integer, commonly 5 to 12
keys.effect: Higher keeps more verbatim recent history at the cost of summarising the rest more aggressively; lower trims harder and forgets older nuance sooner.
keys.gotcha: Set it too low and Evy forgets what you just discussed right when she compresses memory.

keys.label: Max tools per load_skills
keys.what: The ceiling on secondary tools Evy may pull in during a single load_skills call.
keys.values: An integer, commonly 5 to 15
keys.effect: Higher lets Evy arm herself with more capabilities at once, using more of the static budget; lower keeps her focused and lean but she may need extra load steps.
keys.gotcha: Cranking it up eats into your static token slice and can crowd out instructions.

keys.label: Headless browser (default)
keys.what: Whether Playwright automation runs invisibly or with a visible browser window.
keys.values: true = hidden; false = you can watch it work
keys.effect: Headless is faster and stays out of the way; visible is invaluable for debugging a flaky site or seeing exactly what Evy does.
keys.gotcha: On some sites a visible browser passes bot checks that a headless one fails.

keys.label: Thinking (reasoning tokens)
keys.what: Turns on the model's reasoning-token phase before it answers.
keys.values: true or false
keys.effect: On gives more deliberate, accurate answers on hard problems at the cost of latency and tokens; off makes Evy reply faster and cheaper.
keys.gotcha: Turning Thinking off in the TUI also disables stream_thinking, so the two travel together.

keys.label: Stream thinking to UI
keys.what: Shows the reasoning tokens live in the terminal UI as Evy thinks.
keys.values: true or false
keys.effect: On lets you watch her work and catch bad reasoning early; off keeps the display clean and just shows the final answer.
keys.gotcha: It does nothing when Thinking is disabled, since there are no reasoning tokens to show.

keys.label: Home directory (security boundary)
keys.what: The root directory Evy is allowed to touch with her file tools.
keys.values: An absolute path, e.g. /Users/you/Documents
keys.effect: All file read, write, list, and grep operations are confined beneath this path. Widening it gives Evy more reach; narrowing it fences her in.
keys.gotcha: Point it at your whole home folder and you have handed a clever assistant the keys to everything you own.

keys.label: Git user name
keys.what: The author name attached to git commits Evy makes.
keys.values: Any string
keys.effect: Shows up as the commit author, so choose a name you are happy to see in your history.
keys.gotcha: A careless value makes Evy's commits look like they came from a stranger.

keys.label: Git user email
keys.what: The author email attached to git commits Evy makes.
keys.values: Any email address, ideally one tied to your git host account
keys.effect: Determines whether commits link to a real account and show up as yours.
keys.gotcha: A wrong email means your git host will not associate Evy's commits with you.

keys.label: Control panel port
keys.what: The local port this setup panel is served on.
keys.values: An integer port, commonly 8765
keys.effect: Changes the URL you use to reach the panel, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8765. Picked up when the panel starts.
keys.gotcha: If another app already owns the port, the panel fails to bind until you change it.

keys.label: Setup complete
keys.what: The first-run flag that tells Evy setup has been finished.
keys.values: true or false
keys.effect: When false, Evy shows the first-run splash and opens this panel automatically; when true, she boots straight into normal operation.
keys.gotcha: It also flips to true as soon as any secret is saved, so a half-finished setup can look complete.

keys.label: Ollama API key
keys.what: The credential Evy uses to reach Ollama's cloud API at ollama.com.
keys.values: A key created in your Ollama account; leave blank in local mode
keys.effect: Required whenever Mode is cloud, and for cloud-backed Q&A and summarisation. In local mode it is safely unused.
keys.gotcha: Cloud mode with this blank means no brain at all, which is a quiet way to break the whole assistant.

keys.label: Preconscious key
keys.what: A separate API key used for Evy's heartbeat and scheduled autonomous runs.
keys.values: A key from your model provider; blank falls back to the main key
keys.effect: Keeps background heartbeat traffic on its own quota so it does not interfere with your live conversation session. Handy for billing separation and rate limits.
keys.gotcha: Leaving it blank is fine, but all traffic then shares one key and one quota.

keys.label: Discord bot token
keys.what: The bot token that lets Evy read and respond to Discord messages.
keys.values: A bot token from https://discord.com/developers/applications
keys.effect: With it, Evy can monitor channels, reply, and send proactive updates; the header also reflects the connection. Without it, Discord tools are inert.
keys.gotcha: A token with the wrong intents enabled connects but silently never sees messages.

keys.label: Notion integration token
keys.what: The internal integration token for reading and writing Notion pages and databases.
keys.values: A token starting with ntn_, from https://www.notion.so/my-integrations
keys.effect: Enables Notion read, write, and database tools. The integration must also be shared with each page you want Evy to touch.
keys.gotcha: A valid token still sees nothing until you invite the integration into the specific pages.

keys.label: Notion default page ID
keys.what: The parent page under which Evy creates new Notion pages by default.
keys.values: A Notion page ID (the 32-character id from the page URL)
keys.effect: Lets Evy file new pages without asking where each time. Without it she must be told a parent on every create.
keys.gotcha: If the parent page is not shared with the integration, creation fails even though the token is valid.

keys.label: Tavily API key
keys.what: The key for Tavily, the AI-optimised web search Evy uses.
keys.values: A key starting with tvly-, from https://app.tavily.com
keys.effect: Enables live web search so Evy can answer with current information instead of only her training data.
keys.gotcha: Without it Evy cannot search the web at all and will say so when asked about anything recent.

keys.label: Obsidian host
keys.what: The local address of the Obsidian Local REST API plugin.
keys.values: A URL such as http://127.0.0.1:27123
keys.effect: Points Evy at your vault's HTTP bridge so she can read, write, and search notes. It is local, not a secret in the usual sense, though it lives with the secrets.
keys.gotcha: The plugin must be running and listening on this exact address, or every Obsidian tool times out.

keys.label: Obsidian API key
keys.what: The key issued by the Obsidian Local REST API plugin.
keys.values: The API key shown in the plugin settings
keys.effect: Authenticates Evy to your vault so she can modify notes, not just reach the server.
keys.gotcha: Wrong key returns 401s that can look like the plugin is down.

keys.label: GitHub token
keys.what: A GitHub personal access token for repository actions.
keys.values: A PAT with repo scope, from https://github.com/settings/tokens
keys.effect: Lets Evy create pull requests and act against your GitHub repos, beyond what local git can do. Plain local commits do not need it.
keys.gotcha: Too narrow a scope makes push or PR actions fail with permission errors.

keys.label: Groq API key (voice)
keys.what: The key for Groq's Orpheus text-to-speech used by voice mode.
keys.values: A key from https://console.groq.com/keys
keys.effect: Enables Ctrl+V voice mode, where Evy speaks replies aloud in short conversational sentences. Without it voice mode has no voice.
keys.gotcha: Voice mode also reshapes Evy's replies into chatty sentences, which is jarring if you were expecting tables and code.

keys.label: Email connections
keys.what: One or more mailbox connections, each an email address, app password, and description.
keys.values: Gmail address plus an app password (not your main password) and a short purpose note
keys.effect: Stored in credentials/emails.json and injected into Evy's context, so she knows which mailboxes exist, what each is for, and can send and read mail.
keys.gotcha: Gmail requires a generated app password and 2FA enabled, or authentication will fail repeatedly.
